caption: Three kids between us and a maintenance payment neither of us says out loud at dinner. Does blending finances get easier, or do you just get used to it?

slides.title:
How we spend
our R38 500
household income
Living in Richards Bay
slides.body:
Him 38, her 35
Blended family, three kids between us
Jobs: Boilermaker at the smelter & admin clerk
Combined net: R38 500 p/m

slides.title: Bond repayment
slides.includes: 3 bed, bought before we got together, now home to all three kids
slides.body: He owned it first. My name went on it the year we moved in properly.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Feeding five most weeks, three every other weekend
slides.body: The trolley changes size depending on whose custody weekend it is.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: Bakkie for his shift changeovers at the smelter
slides.body: Non-negotiable when the shift starts at 5am and the taxis haven't.

slides.title: School fees & stationery
slides.body: Two school terms, two uniform lists, one budget that pretends it's one family.

slides.title: Maintenance to his ex
slides.includes: Goes to his two kids' mother every month, on top of what they cost here
slides.body: Nobody posts this line. It's real and it's not going anywhere.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Electricity, medical aid for three kids, petrol, phone & fibre, funeral policy, a stokvel we can't miss a month on, savings
slides.body: Eight small debit orders between two households. We only added them up properly for this.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R38 500, across five people some weekends and three the rest of the time. Thinner than either of our old single budgets.

slides.title: I stopped assuming our numbers matched
slides.body:
We uploaded both our statements to Beyond Horizon and split the categories properly for the first time.

The maintenance line had never been in either of our old budgets — now it's just a line, not a surprise.

No bank login needed.
